  "content": "# Remote-sensing inputs for the 3I/ATLAS solar-wind model

Downloaded 2026-10-16/17. Everything here is public and needs no account. Total size is about 300 MB. The scripts live in `scripts_rs/` and run as `python -I scripts_rs/<name>.py` (sunpy env: `/home/scabot/miniconda3/envs/mhd_claude/bin/python`):

| script | what it does |
|---|---|
| `fetch_maps.py gong adapt wsa wsavel wsaadapt ensemble` | daily map downloads, one file per day closest to 00 UT (within ±12 h), 2025-10-15 to 2025-12-06 |
| `index_maps.py` | writes the `index.csv` files from the FITS headers |
| `ephem_heeq.py` | JPL Horizons vectors (Sun-centered ICRF) converted to HEEQ (HGS) and Earth-view Carrington longitude, 3-hourly from 2025-10-15 to 2025-12-12 |
| `cme_geometry.py` | tidies DONKI, compares it with the CCMC cone list, and checks cone geometry and arrival at the comet |
| `qc_plots.py` | QC PNGs, the data-age table, the comet source-longitude table, and the WSA layout check |

## 1. GONG mrzqs (`gong/`, 53 files, 13 MB)

- Source: `https://gong.nso.edu/data/magmap/QR/zqs/YYYYMM/mrzqsYYMMDD/mrzqsYYMMDDtHHMMcCRRR_LLL.fits.gz`. This is the hourly, zero-point-corrected, QuickReduce (QR) standard synoptic map. `LLL` in the name is the left-edge longitude.
- Layout: a single primary HDU of 360 x 180 float32 in Gauss. It is Carrington cylindrical equal-area, so axis 2 is sine(latitude) with `CDELT2 = 1/90`. Pixel-center longitude is `CRVAL1 + (i+1-CRPIX1)*CDELT1` (0-based i), which runs from `LONG0 + 0.5` to `LONG0 + 359.5`. The map is not wrapped to 0-360.
- Time and longitude keywords:
  - `MAPDATE`/`MAPTIME`: the UT of the last contributing magnetogram.
  - `CAR_ROT`: the rotation of longitude 0 of the map.
  - `MAPL0`: the Earth central-meridian (CM) longitude at map time.
  - `LONG0` = `MAPEDGE`: the left (leading) edge longitude, which is 60° east of CM.
  - `CRNOW` and `CR60`: fractional Carrington-rotation numbers for "now" and for the point 60° in.
  - `CRVAL1A`/`CDELT1A`: the fractional-rotation axis.
  - Following the header COMMENT, the 60° of the map to the left of `MAPL0` has not yet crossed CM.
- `index.csv` columns: file, map_time_utc, carrington_rotation, cr_lon_at_map_time (= MAPL0), crnow, left_edge_lon, nfiles, image_mean_G.
- Gaps: none at daily cadence. The nearest-to-00 UT pick is the previous day's 23:24/23:34 file for 2025-11-19, 11-21 and 12-04, and 2025-10-14 21:14 for 2025-10-15.
- `FILELIST` in each mrzqs header points to the matching `mrzql` file. WSA reads that file, as the WSA headers below show.

## 2. ADAPT-GONG (`adapt/`, 53 files, 158 MB)

- Source: `https://gong.nso.edu/adapt/maps/gong/2025/adapt40311_044012_YYYYMMDD0000_<lastobs>.fts.gz`. All of these are the 00 UT maps. The naming follows the NSO ADAPT readme:
  - `4`: public.
  - `0`: Carrington-fixed frame. A twin `adapt41311` series uses the CM-centered frame.
  - `3`: GONG input.
  - `1`: enLS data assimilation.
  - `1`: 1° resolution.
  - `04 4`: code version.
  - `012`: realizations.
  - The tail `TIIJJKKLLGQ` gives the evolution mode and the time since the last assimilated observation.
- Layout: HDU0 is (12, 180, 360) float32 in Gauss, one plane per realization. Latitude is equal-angle, from -89.5 to 89.5. Longitude is Carrington-fixed with pixel centers 0.5 to 359.5 (`CRVAL1=180` at `CRPIX1=180.5`). The other HDUs are:
  - HDU1 `ensemParmInfo`: per-realization supergranulation, meridional-flow, differential-rotation and random-flux parameters.
  - HDU2/3: ensemble statistics.
  - HDU4 `STDDEV`: the 12-member standard-deviation map.
- Keywords:
  - `MAPTIME`, `MAPJUL`.
  - `MAPLON`/`MAPCR`: CM longitude and rotation at map time.
  - `LAST_OBS`: days since the last assimilated magnetogram.
  - `NREAL`, `COVERAGE`.
  - `FLUXSCAL = 1.8`: a scaling applied to the input GONG data.
  - `CRLNGEDG`/`CRROTEDG`: the WSA leading edge.
- `index.csv` columns: file, map_time_utc, carrington_rotation, map_cr, cr_lon_at_map_time, nreal, last_obs_days, coverage_pct, fluxscal, modelver.
- **Major caveat:** the archived ADAPT-GONG run assimilated no data from 2025-10-08 15:04 UT to 2025-11-18 ~22 UT. `LAST_OBS` climbs from 6.4 d on Oct 15 to 40.4 d on Nov 18, then resets to 0.09 d on Nov 19. The `adapt41311` twin has the same tags. The NSO files were rewritten on 2026-03-02, and GONG mrzqs kept updating normally over that interval.
  - Consequence: on 2025-11-25 the ADAPT maps hold fresh data only over roughly 0-150° Carrington longitude. That is the disk seen since Nov 19; the STDDEV plane shows it as a low-variance disk. Longitudes ~150-360° hold flux-transported data from before Oct 8, about 47-75 days old.
  - In the GONG map the same far-side longitudes show active regions observed in mid-November (lon 230-290). The two inputs will give different global PFSS/HCS solutions.
  - The real-time iSWA ADAPT-WSA outputs (below) were computed in Nov 2025 from the ADAPT run as it stood then. I did not check whether that run assimilated data during the gap.

## 3. SDO/HMI (`hmi/`, 8 files, 22 MB)

- Source: `https://jsoc1.stanford.edu/data/hmi/synoptic/`, static files with no account needed.
- `hmi.Synoptic_Mr_small.2302..2305.fits`: 720 x 360 sine-lat, 0.5° in longitude, in Mx/cm².
- `hmi.Synoptic_Mr_polfil.2302..2305.fits`: 3600 x 1440 polar-filled maps, tile-compressed (CompImageHDU in astropy).
- Keywords:
  - `CRVAL1`/`CDELT1` are Carrington time in degrees, CR*360 − lon, so `CDELT1 < 0` means longitude increases to the right.
  - `CAR_ROT`.
  - `T_START`/`T_STOP` in TAI.
  - `LON_FRST`/`LON_LAST`.
- Daily-updated HMI maps (`hmi.mrdailysynframe_720s`) exist statically only as the latest NRT frame. Historical frames need a JSOC export, which requires a registered e-mail, so I skipped them.

## 4. CCMC WSA 5.4 / GONGz (`wsa_ccmc/`, 96 MB)

- **Obtainable.** The FITS behind the CCMC run's boundary list (`/wsadw_5.4/gongz/YYYY/MM/wsadw_gongz_YYYYMMDDTHHMM.fits`) are mirrored on iSWA as `https://iswa.gsfc.nasa.gov/iswa_data_tree/model/solar/WSA5.4/R21.5/WSA_OUT/GONG_Z/YYYY/MM/wsa_YYYYMMDDHHMMR000_gong_z.fits`.
  - Every one of the 2359 boundary-list timestamps exists on iSWA; iSWA has 3 extra.
  - I did not byte-compare the files with the CCMC copies, because the RoR `run_files.php` listing holds only the boundary PNGs and the ENLIL netCDF, not the FITS. The run's netCDF header confirms `corona=WSA_V5.4`, `observatory=gongz`, `cordata=wsadw_5.4`.
  - The iSWA hourly series has a gap from 2025-11-09 02:14 to 2025-11-10 16:14. The CCMC boundary list has the same gap. The 2025-11-10 entry is therefore the 16:14 file.
- `wsa_*_gong_z.fits` (53 files). HDU0 is (8, 90, 180) float32 on a 2° grid. Rows are `lat_j = -89 + 2j`; columns are `lon_i = CARRLONG + 1 + 2i`. I confirmed this independently by sampling the GONG mrzqs map onto the WSA grid (`qc/wsa_layout_check.csv`): photospheric-field correlation is r = 0.91 with point sampling; flipping latitude gives 0.02; dropping CARRLONG gives 0.14. The eight planes:
  1. Br at RADOUT = 21.5 Rs (nT).
  2. Expansion factor fs at the source surface.
  3. Footpoint colatitude (rad).
  4. Footpoint longitude (rad; take |value| and add CARRLONG).
  5. Photospheric Br (G).
  6. θb, the footpoint distance to the nearest coronal-hole boundary (deg).
  7. Open/closed flag.
  8. Distance to the current sheet at the outer boundary (deg).
- Other HDUs:
  - HDU1 (7, 3, 180): the same quantities along the sub-Earth track.
  - HDU2 (4, 180): sub-Earth colatitude, longitude, radius and JD.
  - HDU3 (2, 91, 91): PFSS g/h coefficients in µT, Schmidt-normalized, WSO convention.
- WSA header keywords:
  - `CARROT`/`CARRLONG`: leading-edge rotation and longitude, which is CM − 60°.
  - `OBSTIME`, `OBSJUL`, `OBSLON`, `OBSCAR`: the latest magnetogram at CM.
  - `RADSS = 2.51`, `RADINT = 2.49`, `RADOUT = 21.5`: the Schatten current-sheet model is used from 2.49 Rs.
  - `SPHHAR = 90`.
  - `MPCORR = 2`: scaled monopole correction, with `MPOLD` and `MPNEW`.
  - `FILELIST = mrzqlYYMMDDtHHMMcCRRR_LLL`.
  - `MAPTYPE = DU`: daily updated.
- `vel/vel_*_gongz.fits` (53 files, from `.../WSA_VEL/GONG_Z/`). HDU0 is (2, 90, 180) on the same grid: plane 1 is Br at 21.5 Rs (nT), plane 2 is the WSA speed (km/s). The header gives the velocity law verbatim: `VELEQN = 285.0+625.0/((1.0+fexp)**0.22222) * (1.0-0.8*exp(-(arc_ft_bd/2.0)**2.0))**3.0`.
- `adapt_wsa/` (75 files): iSWA real-time WSA 5.4 driven by ADAPT-GONG (`.../WSA_OUT/ADAPT/GONG/`, `wsa_YYYYMMDDHHMMR0NN_agong.fits`). There is one realization-0 file per day, plus all 12 realizations for 2025-11-25 00 UT and 2025-12-03 00 UT. The layout is the same as GONGz plus an `ensemParmInfo` table. `CARRLONG` here is not CM − 60°: it is 247° on Nov 25, the ADAPT leading-edge convention. Use the per-file `CARRLONG`. Nov 10 is missing (an iSWA gap). Cadence is irregular, 2-6 h.
- Each subfolder has an `index.csv` with these columns: file, ccmc_boundary_name, map_time_utc, carrington_rotation, carrlong_leading_edge, obscar, cr_lon_at_map_time, filelist, observatory, radss, radout, provers, mpold_G, realiz.
- `enlil_run/` holds outputs of the reviewer's CCMC run Jan_Deca_120925_SH_1, from `https://ccmc.gsfc.nasa.gov/ror/api/get_run_file.php?runnumber=Jan_Deca_120925_SH_1&filename=...`:
  - `evo.3I-Atlas_CME_estimates_2AU.nc` (the top-level `evo.3I-Atlas.nc` kept returning HTTP 500; the `CME_estimates/2AU/` copy downloaded), `evo.stereoa.nc`, `evo.earth.nc`, `ror_metadata.json`.
  - The netCDF variables are D (kg/m³), T (K), V1-3 (m/s), B1-3 (T), DP and BP. Each has two columns: column 0 is the run with cone clouds and DP is the cloud tracer.
  - Coordinates are HEEQ+180. Time is in seconds from 2025-10-01T00.
  - The global attributes record the a6b1 boundary actually used: `boundary_old = "B=350./4./0./1 D=125./2. T=1.5/0 V=700./25./75./200. S=9. A=0.05"`, `parameters = "g=1.6666667 q=0.05/1 xa=0.05"`, `rbnd = 0.1 AU`, `crpos = 2302_074`.
  - At the comet during the XMM window this run gives about 406-411 km/s and n_p ≈ 1.0-1.1 cm⁻³ (D/m_p/1.2), with no cloud material (DP ~ 0).

## 5. CMEs (`cme/`)

- `donki_cme_analysis.json`: CMEAnalysis, mostAccurateOnly=true, 2025-10-15 to 2025-12-06, 289 analyses of 261 CMEs.
  - The API host that answered was `https://ccmc.gsfc.nasa.gov/DONKI/WS/get/...`. `kauai.ccmc.gsfc.nasa.gov` resolves to IPv6 only and is unreachable from this machine; `api.nasa.gov` returned 503.
  - A CME can have two "most accurate" analyses: one for the leading edge (LE) and one for the shock (SH).
- `donki_cme_analysis_all.json`: all analyses.
- `donki_cme.json`: CME records with source location, notes, linked events and per-analysis ENLIL impacts.
- `donki_wsaenlil.json`, `donki_ips.json` (interplanetary shocks), `donki_flr.json`.
- `donki_cme_analysis.csv` columns: cme_id (DONKI activity ID), time21_5, lat_heeq, lon_heeq (Stonyhurst/HEEQ, + = west), half_width, speed, type, feature_code, technique, catalog, source_location, active_region, instruments, analysis_link, in_ccmc_list.
- `ccmc_vs_donki.csv`: the CCMC cone list joined to DONKI by activity ID. Every CCMC entry in the fetch range matches a DONKI most-accurate analysis exactly; the CCMC list keeps the LE or SH analysis, v ≥ 600 km/s and half-width ≥ 30°.
- `ephem_heeq.csv`: HEEQ r, lon, lat and Earth-view Carrington longitude for the comet (Horizons `C/2025 N1`, JPL#54), Earth, STEREO-A, Solar Orbiter and PSP.
- `cme_comet_geometry.csv`: for every DONKI and CCMC cone, the axis-to-comet separation and the arrival at the comet. The model:
  - The cone axis is fixed in inertial space, so it drifts −0.986°/day in HEEQ.
  - Arrival is computed three ways: constant speed, drag-based model (DBM: γ = 0.2×10⁻⁷ km⁻¹, w = 400 km/s, from 21.5 Rs), and DBM with an ice-cream-cone front, r(δ)/R = [cos δ + √(sin²w − sin²δ)]/(1 + sin w).
  - "plus15" lets the shock extend 15° beyond the DONKI half-width.

There are 92 entries for Nov 1-Dec 6. P-points lie at r ≤ 1 AU and mostly at HLO within ±80° of Earth, often at high latitude.

## Caveats

- Ballistic mapping ignores acceleration inside 0.1 AU, stream interaction and the latitudinal footpoint offset. Source longitudes are good to about ±15°.
- The DBM parameters are generic. DONKI cone parameters come from SWPC_CAT fits, and several near-limb or far-side events were fit from GOES CCOR-1 alone (for example 2025-11-23T23:30).
- Solar Orbiter was at HEEQ +15° and latitude +10° in Nov 2025. PHI-FDT BLOS (L2/L3, 184 files, 2025-11-02 to 12-03, on SOAR) therefore adds only about 15° of west-limb view and no far-side coverage. I did not download it.
- The IPS-CAT start CR is inferred. The VLIST P-points do not sample the comet's sector beyond 1 AU.
- ADAPT `FLUXSCAL = 1.8` means ADAPT-GONG field strengths are not directly comparable with mrzqs.
